entries.title: 📱 The clip that will not die
entries.text: One week later the eleven words are still everywhere: reaction videos, remixes, a late-night monologue. {client} has stopped reading the mentions. The question on your desk: feed the fire, starve it, or redirect it.

quest.title: Kill the viral clip
quest.step: Decide how to fight the {client} clip

choices.label: Own it — a fast, human apology video

effects.text: {client} posts the apology video. Now the internet decides what it was worth.

choices.outcome: Ninety unscripted seconds, posted before the lawyers could object. The comments split — but the tone shifts a degree.

choices.label: Ignore it — the feed always moves on

effects.text: No statement on the {client} clip. You bet on the internet's short memory.

choices.outcome: Silence as strategy. It works more often than the commentators admit — and fails more loudly.

entries.title: 📱 Two weeks later: the clip's afterlife
entries.text: The analytics are in. The clip peaked, dipped, twitched — and now hangs at the edge of the feed, waiting for a reason to come back. One good story would bury it for good.

quest.step: Bury the clip under a better story

choices.label: Feed the algorithm a better {client} story

effects.text: The new {client} story that finally retired the clip
A better story buries the clip. The feed has a new toy.

choices.outcome: A charity visit, genuinely moving, expertly filmed. By Sunday the clip is a footnote to a better story.

effects_fail.text: The counter-story reads as damage control — and revives the clip instead.

choices.outcome_fail: The planted story smells planted. The clip returns for a victory lap, now with commentary about the cover-up.

choices.label: Let it burn out on its own

effects.text: The clip fades on its own schedule, taking a little of {client}'s heat with it.

choices.outcome: It fades. They always fade. What lingers is a faint asterisk next to {client}'s name in the feed's memory.
